status: Factory/caps, GDI allocation identity, descriptor bridge and primary mode-state corrections implemented. All applicable original Wine conformance remains incomplete.
changes: Default/HARDWAREONLY/EMULATIONONLY factories preserve their selected profile. HEL defaults to system storage, rejects explicit video requests and unsupported 24-bit depth. Disabled HAL and HEL cap records retain distinct native conventions; caller-size bounds remain.

GetGDISurface follows the original allocation through real flip storage exchanges. FlipToGDISurface selects that allocation via the existing Flip implementation with native errors for absent, standalone and lost primary surfaces. This is allocation identity metadata coverage, not a new GDI desktop pixel certificate.

Managed SetSurfaceDesc is rejected without mutation. Failed D3D7 EndStateBlock preserves the output handle. Old depth descriptors use DDSD_ZBUFFERBITDEPTH and the old depth union, not DDSD_PIXELFORMAT; converting old depth input clears the modern mip-count union. All primary views expose live display depth while allocation dimensions and pitch remain immutable.

Native primary markers remain window/loss controllers. A desktop primary uses the actual screen DC dimensions/depth after native preparation; an explicitly selected DDraw mode survives temporary desktop restoration during focus loss. Lost primary Restore validates the public pixel allocation against the effective mode before calling Native Restore, since a different-sized private marker cannot validate the allocation.

Local full-suite startup records and closes only recognized XP boot-time PnP dialogs, waits for a quiet desktop, then terminates before Wine starts. No setup input runs during a test. Original Wine assertions and executable source are unchanged.
